title: Permission-Filtered RAG & GraphRAG
tagline: Retrieval that checks permissions before it ranks: exact tenant isolation, document ACLs, hybrid search, a citation on every sentence, multi-hop graph paths, and an honest 'I don't know'.
why: The fastest way to lose an enterprise customer is a chatbot that quotes the CEO's salary to an intern, or another customer's data to a tenant. Filtering after retrieval is not enough: a hidden document can still shape scores, snippets and counts. This repo applies tenant and ACL checks before anything is ranked, grounds every answer sentence in a cited chunk, and abstains when the evidence is weak.
covers: Pre-retrieval filter: exact tenant match, user / group ACL, explicit deny, tenant-wide flag that never crosses tenants, tag filters
Hybrid search: sentence-aware chunking, BM25, hashed character-trigram vectors, Reciprocal Rank Fusion
Extractive answers with a [doc#chunk] citation per sentence and a verbatim grounding check
Abstention when term coverage or lexical evidence is below a threshold
GraphRAG: shortest multi-hop path over triples; each edge inherits its source document's ACL
Leak test: proves no out-of-scope document is returned and lists what the filter blocked
gaps: Hashed n-gram vectors stand in for a real embedding model; swap search::vector for your embeddings
No LLM generation step: answers are extractive, which is what makes the grounding check exact
No persistent index or vector DB; documents are passed in per request
Triple extraction from text (entity / relation NER) is not included; triples are inputs

ops.label: Hybrid search
ops.help: Bo (support, tenant acme) searches for hotel limits. The exec and Globex policies match the words but are filtered out before ranking: visible_docs shows only what Bo may see.
